rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: Paris, 1858, in a box at the Opera. Paul Morphy, with White, played the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard together.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.e2: Morphy has just given up his queen on b8, and the knight captured it. The black king is on e8, and the bishop on g5 watches the diagonal up to d8.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks on d8, next to the king, and the bishop on g5 supports it. The king cannot capture it.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes to d8 and gives mate: it stands next to the king, and the bishop on g5 supports it along the diagonal.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d7.1: The rook goes to d7, next to the king, but without check and without support: none of your pieces defends that square.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d7.2: With this move Black has a resource: the king captures the rook, because it had no support.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d7.3: Back to the position: look for the square next to the king that your bishop supports.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d6.1: The rook attacks the queen on e6, but without check, and it lands on a square the bishop on f8 watches.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d6.2: With this move Black has a resource: the bishop on f8 captures the rook, and the attack is over.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.err.d1d6.3: Back to the position: before attacking the queen, look for the check with support.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not give mate, and Black, a queen up, defends. Look for the rook check that the bishop supports.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the bishop on g5 watches d8; look for the rook check.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.l1: This is the Opera mate, named after this game: the rook mates next to the king, and the bishop supports it from afar.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex1.l2: The bishop also covers e7, and the rook covers d7. For the support to work, the bishop's diagonal must be open up to the mating square.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the black king is on g8, behind the pawns on f7 and g7. The pawn on h6 has opened the square h7 for it.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.e2: Your bishop on d3 watches the diagonal up to h7, and your rook on c1 has the c-file open up to the eighth rank.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks from afar, on c8, and the bishop on d3 takes the square h7 from the king.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.revela: The rook goes to c8 and gives mate: the check comes along the eighth rank, and the bishop on d3 covers h7, the escape square.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.c1c5.1: The rook attacks the knight on e5, but without check, and the knight still attacks your bishop on d3.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.c1c5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the knight captures the bishop, and the black king gains the square h7.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.c1c5.3: Back to the position: leave the bishop watching h7 and give check with the rook.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3f5.1: The bishop goes to f5 without check, and Black gains a tempo.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3f5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook goes to c4 and offers a trade. Without your rook, there is no mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3f5.3: Back to the position: on d3 the bishop already covers h7. Look for the rook check.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.1: The bishop goes to e2 without check and leaves the h7 diagonal.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook attacks the pawn on a2. Without the bishop on d3, the check on c8 is no longer mate: the king escapes to h7.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.3: Back to the position: leave the bishop on d3, watching h7, and give check with the rook.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not give mate, and Black gains time to defend. Look for the rook check on the eighth rank.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the bishop covers h7; look for the rook check on the eighth.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.l1: This is Pillsbury's mate: the rook checks from afar, and the bishop takes the escape square from the king.
rot.rookBishopMates.ideia.ex2.l2: In the Opera mate, the bishop supports the rook next to the king; in Pillsbury's, it covers the escape. In both, rook and bishop work together.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.1: Attack: your rook on h1 has the h-file open up to the black bishop on h8, and your bishop on d4 watches the same square.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.p: Find the move that gives mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook captures the bishop with check, next to the king, and the bishop on d4 supports it and covers g7.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.revela: The rook captures on h8 and gives mate: the bishop on d4 supports it, and the king cannot capture it.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.err.d4h8: The bishop captures the one on h8 without check, and Black gains a tempo.
With this move Black has a resource: the pawn goes to f6 and traps your bishop on h8. Black stays a queen up.
Back to the position: capture on h8 with the piece that leaves the bishop as support.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.err.e1c1: Castling brings the other rook to d1, but it is not a check.
With this move Black has a resource: the bishop on h8 captures yours on d4, and the mate is gone.
Back to the position: look for the check with the rook on h1.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.opera.2: The king has no square: the bishop covers g7, and the rook covers f8. It is the Opera mate, with the bishop supporting from afar, on d4.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.1: Attack: the black king is on f8, and a rook check on e8 does not work now: the king would capture it.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.p: Find the bishop check that prepares the mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.cert: Yes: the bishop checks on h6 and covers g7. The rook on e1 covers e7 and e8, and the king only has g8.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.reve: The bishop goes to h6 with check: it covers g7, the rook covers e7 and e8, and the king only has g8.
The rook checks on e8, next to the king, but without support.
With this move Black has a resource: the king captures the rook, and you are left with the bishop only.
Back to the position: first drive the king away from e8, with a bishop check.
The king goes to b6 without check, and Black gains a tempo.
With this move Black has a resource: the king goes to g7 and leaves the eighth rank. Black stays three pawns up.
Back to the position: every tempo counts. Start with the bishop check.
The bishop checks on e7, but from there it does not cover g7.
With this move Black has a resource: the king goes to g7 and leaves the eighth rank. Black stays three pawns up.
Back to the position: look for the bishop check that also covers g7.
The bishop goes to f6 and covers g7, but without check, and Black gains a tempo.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook goes to f4 and attacks your bishop. Black stays three pawns up.
Back to the position: look for the bishop check that covers g7.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.2: The king goes to g8, because it has no other square. Now the square e8 is far from it.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.3: The rook mates on e8, from afar, and the bishop on h6 covers g7: it is Pillsbury's mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.pillsbury.4: Here the bishop gave the first check and drove the king to the square where the rook reaches it from afar.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.1: Attack: your bishop on d6 watches f8, and the rook on f1 could give the Opera mate there.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.2: But the square f8 is defended: the rook on e8 defends it, and the knight on f6 blocks the f-file.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.p: With a queen check, pull the rook on e8 away from the defence of f8. Find the move.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.certo: Yes, the queen captures the rook on e8 with check. See why it forces mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.revela: The move is the queen to e8: it captures the rook with check, and Black has to capture it with the knight.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.err.c8: The queen checks on e6, but the rook on e8 reaches that square.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook captures the queen, and your attack is over.
Back to the position: look for the check that pulls the rook on e8 away from the defence of f8.
The queen attacks the knight on f6, but without check, and Black gains a tempo.
With this move Black has a resource: the pawn goes to h6 and gives the king the square h7. The game is balanced.
Back to the position: before the mate on f8, pull the rook on e8 away from the defence.
The queen captures the pawn on b7, but without check, and the square f8 is still defended.
With this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the pawn on c2, and the knight still blocks the f-file.
Back to the position: look for the check that removes the defence of f8.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.3: The knight captures the queen: Black has no other move. Now the f-file is open, and nobody defends f8.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.4: The rook mates on f8, next to the king, supported by the bishop on d6: it is the Opera mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.demos.excecao.5: In positions like this, before the mate, check who defends the square. Sometimes giving up the queen removes that defence.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.valeAqui.enu: The black queen threatens mate on g2, but it is your move. Your rook on h1 stands behind the bishop on h4. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The bishop left h4 with check on f6, supported by the rook on f1, and opened the h-file. The king went to g8, and the rook mated on h8, supported by the bishop: the Opera mate. On f7, the rook would have no support.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.valeAqui.err: With 31.Rxf7+, the rook stands next to the king, but none of your pieces supports it on f7: the king captures it, and your attack is over. Then the black queen mates your king.
The bishop captures the one on g3 without check, and Black mates first: the queen captures on g2, supported by the bishop on d5.
The rook attacks the bishop on g3 without check, and Black mates first: the queen captures on g2, supported by the bishop on d5.
The rook blocks the queen's diagonal on f3, but without check: the black queen checks on e1 and reaches your king.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.opera.enunci: The black king is on a6, on the edge. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.opera.fim: The rook captured the one on a7 with mate: next to the king, supported by the bishop on c5. It is the Opera mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.opera.err.c5: The bishop captures the rook on a7 without check, and Black gains time: the rook checks on b1, and the queen joins the attack.
The bishop attacks the rook on b8 without check, and Black gains time: the rook checks on b1 and attacks your king.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.opera.err.f7: The rook retreats to defend the first rank, but it lets the mate on a7 slip away.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.pillsbury.en: Now with Black. The white king is on h1, in the corner. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.pillsbury.fi: The rook mated on f1, from a distance, and the bishop on e5 took the square h2 from the king. It is Pillsbury's mate.
rot.rookBishopMates.pratica.pillsbury.er: The bishop captures the pawn on b2, but it leaves the h2 diagonal. Without it, the check on f1 is no longer mate: the king escapes via h2.
The bishop goes to d4 and leaves the h2 diagonal. Without it, the check on f1 is no longer mate: the king escapes via h2.
The rook leaves the f-file for e8, without check, and White gains time to defend the first rank.
